$comment: Files in src/app allowed to differ from apps/web/src (or to have no web counterpart). One entry per file or glob, relative to src/app. category: platform (a platform service is the reason), native-editor (the native editor is), desktop-only (a screen or tool web has no counterpart for). reason: why, in a sentence. Kit-API drift (onPress, testID, lists, dialogs) is never a reason: phase 4 removes it.

entries.reason: Assets (icons, illustrations, SVG and raster images) generated by tools/gen-assets.mjs, since the GPUI host cannot import asset files the way web's Vite build does.
Smoke screen that exercises every @platform service on the native host; web has no such screen.
Standalone status screen root.tsx shows for the boot/demo mode of the native host; web has no such screen.
Developer benchmarks for the native host (attachment I/O), not part of the app.
Actions the native editor asks its host for (links, attachments, previews); Tiptap does these inside the web editor.
Binds the native editor's host actions to the app's stores and attachment helpers; web's Tiptap editor has no host bridge.

The bug report link opens with the shell service (shell.openUrl); web calls window.open, which the desktop host does not have. The error list also keeps the selectable class so a bug report can copy it: the old desktop code selected it, and web's text is not selectable (app.css only enables selection for the selectable class).
The password field's widest width is 400 where web writes max(30%, 400px): the desktop layout has no CSS min()/max(). Otherwise identical to web.
The filter input is styled through Field's styles.input where web reaches it with an `input` selector in sx: desktop has no stylesheet selectors. Otherwise identical to web.

Web draws PDFs with @react-pdf-viewer (DOM, canvas and its stylesheet); desktop draws them with the kit's PDF viewer over @react-native-gpui/pdf and saves, copies and prints through @platform files, shell and window services.
Web's lightbox is a DOM image viewer that adds a class to document.body and listens for keys on document; desktop draws the image with kit primitives and takes keys from the kit and the window.

Web scrolls the two versions together with react-scroll-sync over DOM scroll containers and renders diffblazer's HTML; desktop has no DOM, so it syncs the kit's scroll views and draws the diff from text.

Web listens for window error and unhandledrejection events, removes the #splash element and reloads with window.location; desktop takes errors from the Hermes runtime and restarts through the lifecycle service.
Web's title bar calls the Electron bridge and window.close; desktop's window controls are the windowControls platform service and the kit's native TitleBar.
Web writes the theme into a <style> element, a theme-color <meta> and the <html> element; desktop has no document and hands the theme to the kit's ThemeScope.
Web picks files with react-dropzone and hashes them with hash-wasm (WebAssembly); desktop picks files with the files platform service and hashes with the crypto service's xxh64.

Web hashes with hash-wasm (WebAssembly) and writes the log with /
and the help link with ; desktop hashes with the crypto service and draws the log as text and the link with the kit.
Web uses a raw <select> and an <a> link; desktop has no HTML elements and uses the kit's Select and a link Text.
Desktop's xxh64 from the crypto platform service, which stands in for hash-wasm (WebAssembly) that the importer uses on web.
Web draws the loading skeleton with react-loading-skeleton (DOM and CSS animation); desktop draws it with kit boxes.
Web lays the calendar out with CSS grid (display: grid) and @rehookify/datepicker; desktop lays out with flexbox only, so the calendar is built from rows.
Web imports the empty-list illustrations as .svg files through Vite; the desktop host cannot import asset files and draws the generated illustrations (illustrations.generated.ts).
Web's icons import @mdi/react and .svg?react files through Vite; desktop draws the same glyphs from the generated paths in icons.generated.ts through the kit's Icon.
Makes the generated desktop icons (see icons.ts); web builds its icons from @mdi/react and SVG components.
Web asks "don't show again" with the synchronous window.confirm; desktop has no blocking browser dialog and asks with ConfirmDialog.
Web takes a pasted code from the input's paste event; the desktop text field raises no paste event, so a pasted code arrives through onChange and is split there.
Web lays action buttons out with CSS grid and opens links with window.open/window.location; desktop lays out with flexbox and opens links with the shell service.
Web shows each bar's tooltip with CSS child selectors (&:hover .tooltip, &:hover .bar) and CSS transition strings; desktop has no stylesheet selectors and uses the kit's hover state on each bar.
Web sizes the switch's label with a `& label` selector; desktop has no stylesheet selectors and styles the label itself.
Web places the background art with CSS grid (justifySelf) and transformOrigin; desktop lays out with flexbox and its transforms always use the element's centre.
Draws the generated SVG and raster assets with the theme's colours; web shows the same files with through Vite, which the desktop host cannot import.
Shows the native window once the first screen has drawn (or after a timeout); a browser tab has no window to reveal.

Web reveals each notebook's add button with CSS child selectors (&:hover .add-sub-notebook, &:focus-within) and styles the list with listStyle; desktop has no stylesheet selectors or list markers and uses the kit's group hover.

Draws its own backdrop and closes on a click there. Web's dialog reads react-modal's DOM (contentEl and offsetLeft/clientWidth geometry) and closes on a mousedown outside that element; the desktop kit's Modal does not expose those, so the close and the layout stay in the desktop file.

Desktop rows are flex layouts, not web's table rows. Attachments are read as base64 (downloadAttachment with base64) and PDFs open as base64 data URLs, because the desktop host has no Blob URLs (web uses URL.createObjectURL). The context menu opens at the pointer through the desktop menu hook.

Keeps the publish form in local state with its own validation and opens the link with shell.openUrl. Web binds the fields with react-hook-form register(), which reads DOM inputs; desktop inputs are native elements, and web's target=_blank anchor has no desktop equivalent.

Uses the desktop ThemeScope in place of web's ScopedThemeProvider and the kit's theme-token colours in place of var(--icon-error). The status icons spin with the kit's rotate prop, and web's responsive display arrays are not drawn.

The spell-check item is not gated on IS_DESKTOP_APP, because the desktop has its own spell checker service. The item gap is a constant rather than a theme lookup, and the list uses the kit's containerSx and placeholderSx props. The collapse caret rotates as on web.

The desktop kit has no alpha() from @theme-ui/color and no CSS hover or transition, so the accent tint comes from a hex colour helper that accepts only #rrggbb and falls back to background-secondary for anything else. The size is split into width and height.

Draws the single-line label with the kit's lineClamp in place of web's CSS ellipsis, and the dismiss control with the kit's secondary button variant. Adds a chip prop with a group-hover background, takes container styles as containerSx, and has no className.

onToggle gets the ctrl or meta state as a boolean, where web passes the DOM event. The label is the element's title, and the unchecked hover colour is the uncheckedGroupHoverColor prop instead of web's CSS class.
onClick gets the ctrl or meta state as a boolean, not the DOM event. The deprecated onPress alias still works, and the click stops at the remove icon.

Renders the desktop MenuHost, which draws the menu panel in the app. Web's wrapper hands the menu to the native shell when it can (use-menu.ts isNative), and the desktop host has no showMenu call, so the menu always draws in the app.

The desktop host for the in-app menu panel. It connects the kit's desktop menu presenter to the menu store and to the @platform keyboard service. Web has no such file: its MenuPresenter is wired in global-menu-wrapper.
Re-exports the kit's shared menu store, which positions the menu from an anchor rectangle, because the desktop kit measures native elements. Web's use-menu store keys the menu on a target element.

Desktop's own lock screen. It unlocks with the native keychain through @platform safeStorage and with WebAuthn security keys through the platform service. Web's lock UI is inline in views/app-lock.tsx and uses the web key store's desktop.safeStorage bridge.
apps/web's split pane is a DOM implementation (CSS class names, window mousemove/mouseup listeners, document.body classList); desktop re-exports the kit's SplitPane and Pane, which resize natively.

apps/web virtualizes with @tanstack/react-virtual on the DOM scroll element it finds with closest('.ms-container') and positions rows with CSS transforms; desktop draws the same list with the kit's Virtuoso on the native list.
apps/web virtualizes with @tanstack/react-virtual on the DOM scroll element it finds with closest('.ms-container'); desktop lays the grid out in rows on the kit's Virtuoso.
apps/web measures its DOM scroll container (closest('.ms-container')) for @tanstack/react-virtual; desktop uses the kit's TableVirtuoso, which owns its native scroll view.

apps/web renders each row in a raw <div> with onMouseUp and finds rows with document.getElementById to focus or click them (waitForElement); desktop has no DOM, so rows register their open action with the kit's list cursor (useListCursor) instead.

apps/web renders raw <div> items and skeletons, finds items with document.querySelector/getElementById (reveal flash with classList, waitForElement focus and click); desktop has no DOM, so items register their open action with the kit's list cursor (useListCursor, kit shared/list-selection.ts) instead.

apps/web measures a paragraph with document.getElementById('p') for the line height and renders items without an index; desktop has no document, so it uses a fixed 16px line and passes each item its list index, which the item registers with the list selection.

apps/web's item takes focus and clicks through the DOM (tabIndex, :focus styles, the focused element); desktop has no DOM, so the item registers its open action and reads the keyboard cursor from the kit's list selection, and carries the e2e markers web reads from the DOM. Native text has no CSS white-space or -webkit-line-clamp, so the title and description use nowrap, lineClamp and px line heights.

apps/web's changeGroupOptions returns early on `!parent` (window.parent, which a browser always sets, so the guard never fires there); desktop has no window, so reading parent would throw, and the guard is left out.
apps/web reads navigator.platform to pick the Mac modifier keys; desktop asks the platform's environment.os, and its key event type also accepts the kit's keyboard event.
apps/web reorders the sidebar with @dnd-kit (DOM pointer sensors and CSS transforms); desktop reorders with the kit's SortableList.
apps/web's SortableNavigationItem is built on @dnd-kit/sortable (DOM); desktop has no such item, the kit's SortableList moves the rows.
apps/web draws the logo from an SVG sprite in index.html (<svg><use href="#full-logo"/>); desktop has no page to hold the sprite, so the mark is an svgIcon here.

The featured-on strip and the testimonials carousel are web's code. The plan cards, pricing and comparison table are still laid out with the kit's flexbox props: web sizes the plan cards from HTMLDivElement measurements and CSS grid, which the desktop layout has no equivalent for.

Web uses CSS grid, a :hover:not(:disabled) selector and DOM input/button refs (inputRef, HTMLInputElement) for the date and time fields; desktop has no grid or selectors and uses the kit's date fields.
Web draws the attachment list as an HTML table (th/td and table sx keys); desktop has no table layout and draws rows with the kit's Virtuoso list.
Web styles the settings rows through child selectors (& > *, & > label), reads inputs with document.getElementById and DOM element refs; desktop has no stylesheet or DOM.
Web imports react-virtuoso directly, highlights matches with <b> elements and sizes with CSS min(); desktop draws through the kit's Virtuoso and Text.

Web uses the phone, file-saver and clipboard-polyfill packages, SVG asset URLs, the react-qrcode-logo re-export, CSS grid, :first-of-type selectors and DOM refs; desktop saves and copies through @platform and draws the QR code with the kit.

Web's toolbar editor reads Tiptap tool definitions from @notesnook/editor and uses document.querySelector, #id hover selectors and :last-of-type; the native editor's toolbar items come from common/toolbar-*.
Web draws the transactions as an HTML table (thead/tbody/th) and opens receipts with window.open; desktop has no table layout and opens links through @platform shell.
Web renders the recovery key to an HTMLCanvasElement, saves it with file-saver and copies with navigator.clipboard and clipboard-polyfill; desktop uses @platform files and clipboard.
Web draws the history as a table (th, td selectors, tableLayout, borderCollapse), sizes text in em and copies with clipboard-polyfill; desktop has no table layout or em units.
Web shows the edit button through a ':hover #profile-picture-edit' selector; desktop has no selectors and uses the kit's group hover.
Web's theme grid uses nested :hover selectors and DOM file reading; desktop draws the grid with the kit and reads files through @platform.
Web embeds Paddle.js checkout in an iframe (@paddle/paddle-js, window.addEventListener, window.location); desktop has no Paddle.js and opens checkout in the browser.
Web passes a DOM input ref to Field (inputRef, HTMLInputElement) and sizes the colour swatch with theme space keys desktop types as lengths; desktop's Field has no inputRef.
Web imports LinkAttributes from @notesnook/editor (Tiptap) and react-virtuoso directly and draws a raw <div>; the native editor takes links through its host actions.
Web reads the fields through DOM input refs (inputRef, HTMLInputElement) on Field; desktop's Field has no inputRef.
Web imports an SVG asset as a URL (rocket.svg?url), uses <span> and the IS_TESTING build global; desktop takes assets from the generated asset modules.

Web copies with clipboard-polyfill, breaks lines with
and uses the forms.input variant path on a textarea; desktop copies through @platform clipboard.
Web uses a native <option> select, navigator.clipboard, a '& + svg' selector and DOM input refs on Field; desktop has none of these.

Web takes the Attachment type from @notesnook/editor (Tiptap), compresses images with its web image-compressor and p-queue on DOM File objects; desktop attaches PickedFile objects to the native editor.
Web reads document.cookie, the service worker registration, navigator.clipboard and window.location/open; desktop has none of these and uses @platform updater, clipboard and shell.
Web crops with react-avatar-editor on a DOM canvas; desktop crops with the kit's AvatarEditor.
Web anchors the date picker popup to a DOM input ref (inputRef, HTMLInputElement) and draws a raw CSS box-shadow; desktop anchors to the kit element and uses the theme's shadow.
Web anchors the date picker popup to a DOM input ref (inputRef, HTMLInputElement) and draws a raw CSS box-shadow; desktop anchors to the kit element and uses the theme's shadow.
Web lays the feature table out with CSS grid and sizes text in rem; desktop lays out with flexbox only.
Web lays the status card out with CSS grid (gridTemplateRows, gridRow); desktop lays out with flexbox only.
Web reads Config.has and the IS_TESTING build global and opens links with window.open; desktop's config has no has() and opens links through @platform shell.
Web passes a DOM input ref to Field (inputRef, HTMLInputElement); desktop's Field has no inputRef.
Web colours the icon through a '& path' selector and uses <strong>; desktop has no selectors and colours the icon directly.
Web registers security keys with the browser's WebAuthn and window.crypto; desktop goes through @platform webauthn, whose calls take different arguments.
Web's Next button submits the 2faForm form in steps.tsx; desktop's steps.tsx (allowlisted) submits through mfa/submit.ts, so the button calls submitStep.
Web reads Vite's import.meta.env.DEV and the IS_TESTING global; desktop reads the same from @platform environment.
The Paddle.js checkout types web imports from @paddle/paddle-js, which desktop does not ship.
The theme listing type web imports from the @notesnook/themes-server package, which desktop-native does not depend on.
What the shared dialogs use outside React on web (the Electron bridge, IS_DESKTOP_APP, getPlatform, window.open/location) implemented on @platform services.
The font list web takes from @notesnook/editor (Tiptap), which the native editor does not ship.
Restart, reload, backup directory and release track calls on @platform for the settings files that are not yet web-identical.
Submits the current MFA step from the dialog's Next button for desktop's steps.tsx, which does not use web's form/id submission.
Desktop stand-ins for what web's dialogs draw with raw HTML or DOM (date input, markdown HTML, radio input, anchored popover, field with DOM refs); used by the allowlisted dialogs.

Hosts the native editor (EditorSurface with its toolbar, host actions and plan permissions) where web mounts Tiptap with its DOM drop zone, scroll restore and search-result scrolling; saveContent, the tabs view, the download progress and the unlock view follow web's.

A heading is reached by asking the native editor to scroll to it (scrollToHeading); web scrolls the DOM node (scrollIntoViewById) and marks the headings in view from the editor's DOM scroll position, which the native editor does not expose.
Turns the plan's features into the command ids the native editor refuses (callout, outline and task lists, attachments, CSV tables); web's Tiptap editor checks them in its own permission handler.

Picked files come from @platform/files (PickedFile) and are hashed from their bytes with the platform's xxh64; web streams a DOM File into hashStream, reads image sizes with an element and queues with p-queue (not a desktop dependency, so a local queue with its API stands in).

Fullscreen goes through @platform windowControls (utils/fullscreen) instead of document.documentElement.requestFullscreen(), hidden tools are left out rather than drawn with display: none (the desktop test driver finds hidden nodes by test id), the word count falls back to counting the stored note until the native editor reports its statistics, the selected-words note is a kit Text instead of a DOM <span>, and the zoom and statistics controls carry the test ids the desktop e2e specs find them by; sx values the kit cannot draw (fit-content, a raw box-shadow, !important) use the nearest tokens.

Desktop's tab strip and tools are written on the kit (SortableList instead of dnd-kit's ReorderableList, @platform window controls and drag data instead of DOM events, no publish tool wiring yet); web's EditorActionBar also reads DOM-only window state. Full alignment is filed as a follow-up.

The kit's native text field is not a DOM textarea: it has no style.height or field-sizing to auto-grow, no selectionDirection, no instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement, no em font sizes or CSS font stacks, and preventDefault on Enter does not stop the newline, so the title is a controlled value that drops newlines and moves focus to the editor on Enter.

Root component of the native host: takes the title-bar inset, waits for the database host (useDatabaseReady), uses the kit's SplitPaneHandle and drops web-only startup code (WebExtensionRelay, console.timeEnd, window focus/fullscreen DOM state).
Native has no HTML form: AuthFormContext carries field values and submit, fields are controlled inputs, and links open through the shell service instead of window.open.
Redirects through hardNavigate (no window.location), since the native host has no browser location.
Waits for the key store to initialize and reveals the window (useWindowReveal) once the lock screen is drawn; password entry is a controlled field because the native host has no input refs.
Checkout page of the native host: validates the plan without zod and draws the logo with <Logo>; web's ReactNativeWebView bridge has no native counterpart.
Paddle's overlay checkout cannot run in the GPUI host: the screen shows a toast and navigates back instead of initializePaddle.
Native has no history.replaceState/window.open (uses hardNavigate) and no <input type=radio> (the radio group is drawn as controls).
React 19 types have no global JSX namespace (ReactNode), and the drop handler receives the platform's UIDataTransfer event.
Opens help links through the shell service rather than window.open.
React 19 types require an initial argument to useRef (useRef<number | undefined>(undefined)).
Reads environment.isDesktopApp instead of the IS_DESKTOP_APP build constant.
Writes through the clipboard service instead of navigator.clipboard.
Reads the location with usePathname from the native navigation instead of wouter's useLocation.
System theme comes from the integration service (getSystemTheme/onSystemThemeChanged), not prefers-color-scheme or the Electron tRPC bridge.
Focus/blur comes from lifecycle.onVisibilityChanged, not window focus/blur events.
Calls the spellChecker service instead of the Electron tRPC client, and re-exports the Language type from the service.
Re-exports the window state hook of the windowControls platform service; web subscribes to the Electron bridge and fullscreenchange.
The native host reports drag enter/leave itself (no DOM bounds or HTMLElement targets), so the hook always reports an enter/leave.
Re-exports the platform's media query hook; the GPUI host has no window.matchMedia.
Hash and query come from the native navigation (getCurrentHash, NavigationEvents) as there is no window.location or hashchange event.
Slides are driven by an index state, not by scroll positions of DOM nodes, since native has no scroll-snap container.
Menus are presented from a native anchor; the Electron native-menu bridge and PositionOptions do not exist.
Closes dialogs on Escape through the native keyboard service; web relies on DOM keydown handlers.
Waits for the database host (whenDatabaseReady) before creating a session; web's database is ready at startup.
Calls integration.changeTheme instead of the Electron tRPC bridge.
Online state comes from lifecycle.isOnline() and fullscreen exit from the windowControls service, not navigator.onLine/document.fullscreenElement.
Session expiry navigates through the native navigation, and the logged-in flag is persisted to Config for the app lock boot path.
Reads environment.platform/os/isTesting and the network policy instead of window.os, PLATFORM and IS_TESTING build constants.
Reminders are delivered through the notifications service instead of the Notification API or the Electron bridge.
Desktop integration, updater and backup directory settings come from the integration/updater services instead of the Electron tRPC client and PATHS.
Tracks the native boot phases (database host, key store) before the app is drawn; web has no boot screen.
The drop event carries the platform's UIDataTransfer, not the DOM DataTransfer.
Reads environment.isDev instead of import.meta.env.DEV.
Reads environment.isTesting/isDesktopApp instead of the build constants IS_TESTING/IS_DESKTOP_APP.
Shortcuts are registered through keyboard.register and the editor check is KeyEvent.inEditor, replacing hotkeys-js and the DOM closest() lookup.
Locale comes from environment.locale; web reads navigator.language and window.appLocale.
Actions wait for the database host; titles are lazy getters so they follow the language; restoreBackupFile takes a PickedFile; IS_* constants are read from environment.
Printing goes through shell.printHtml and files are saved with saveBytes (no iframe, file-saver or Buffer in the host).
A small fetch-based client for the theme server replaces tRPC's browser client, which needs DOM fetch/React Query plumbing.
Exports download for the native editor's temp-file helper, and opens the lightbox with Lightbox.show because the native host has no DOM (no #dialogContainer or ReactDOM.render).
Database key, storage and dialect come from the databaseHost service (WAL, keychain) instead of IndexedDB/OPFS and import.meta.env host overrides.
Thin re-exports of the attachmentFiles platform service (decrypt, upload check, save, temp files); holds no logic of its own.
Placeholder actions for features that web has through browser APIs and native has not built yet.
Toolbar item definitions for the native editor toolbar. The Tiptap toolbar in web is defined inside the editor package.
Icon map for the native editor toolbar. The Tiptap toolbar in web is defined inside the editor package.
Types for the native editor toolbar. The Tiptap toolbar in web is defined inside the editor package.
KVStore contract of @platform/kvStore (async key/value over MMKV); web's IndexedDB-backed interface is not available in the host.
Persists secrets through the platform kvStore/safeStorage (PlatformKVStore) and tracks isInitialized/app-lock state for boot; web uses IndexedDB and CryptoKey storage.
SubtleCrypto subset backed by the native crypto service; web uses window.crypto.subtle.
Saves streams through the files service; web's stream-saver uses a service worker (mitm) download.
All browser feature checks (opfs, indexedDB, clonable CryptoKey, transferable streams) are fixed answers on the native host.
Registration and authentication call the webauthn service instead of navigator.credentials.
Toasts are rendered by the native host, since react-hot-toast is a DOM component library.
Checks and installs updates with the updater service and the network policy instead of the Electron bridge and cookies.
Visibility changes come from lifecycle, not document.hidden and vendor-prefixed events.
Version, hash, platform and beta flag come from environment instead of build-time constants.
Cron tasks run in-process with Cronos; web runs them in a Worker.
Parses HTML with a small DOM-free parser (HtmlNode) since the host has no DOMParser or document.
Reads files from the platform's UIDataTransfer, not the DOM DataTransfer.
Config is stored in the platform config service (MMKV) instead of window.localStorage.
Uses the files service and PickedFile instead of a hidden <input type=file> and File.
The OS comes from environment.os, not the user agent.
Log storage uses databaseHost.createDialect instead of wa-sqlite/OPFS feature checks.
Writes to the clipboard service instead of ClipboardItem/navigator.clipboard.
Adds attributes to HTML with the DOM-free parser in utils/html instead of a detached element.
Waits for the internet through lifecycle.waitForInternet; web uses a Web Worker.
Reads zips from a PickedFile's bytes; ZipEntry is not a Blob in the host.
Attachments are passed as PickedFile and not read into a Uint8Array first.
Fullscreen goes through the windowControls service instead of the DOM fullscreen API.
Creates the file with createPickedFile instead of new File.
Uses the global crypto of the host rather than window.crypto.
Title read/write goes through windowControls and environment.appTitle, not document.title.
Key-up events come from keyboard.onKeyUp, not window.addEventListener.
Email check helper added for native auth forms.
Overlay shown while the native app migrates the Electron database.
Network-disabled switch for the native builds (privacy mode).
Word and character counts are computed here for the native editor; Tiptap exposes them from the editor.
PickedFile, the host's replacement for the browser File.
Replaces date/time placeholders in note content for the native editor, which does not run Tiptap's date/time extension.
Random bytes from the host crypto service.
Startup sequencing for the native host (database, key store).
Synchronous start-up locale for the native boot and the web kit target; web only has the async initLocale.
Decrypts an attachment to a temp file for the native editor's PDF and preview host actions; web's Tiptap editor reads attachments in the page.
Mounts the app on the GPUI host's root view; web renders into a DOM element, lazy-imports a title bar and asks the Electron bridge about it.
Routes hold their components directly because the Hermes bundle cannot lazy-load modules with import(); web's routes are async imports.
Dialogs render into a store-driven host inside the app tree; the GPUI host has no document to createRoot a new container in, as web does.
Navigation goes through the history platform service and wraps its state; web reads window.history and location directly.
Reads history state through the navigation wrapper over the history platform service instead of window.history.
Waits for the database host to be ready before resolving hash routes; web's database is ready at startup.
Waits for the database host and keeps route components with their props because routes are not lazy imports on Hermes.
Link opening and launch requests (nn:// and jump list) come from the integration platform service; web attaches Electron bridge listeners.
Native start-up sequence (database host, key store, locale) that runs before the app mounts on the GPUI host; web boots in root.tsx and index.ts.

Buttons stay disabled and the title waits until the native database host is ready, and the has-items flag is cached in Config so the header does not jump before the lists load; the search field drops web's CSS selector styles (placeholder colour, sibling opacity) the kit has no stylesheet for; route-title and route-action carry test ids for the e2e specs.
Web pads Virtuoso's viewport through a '[data-viewport-type="element"]' selector with a calc() width; desktop has no selectors, so the padding is on the container.
Desktop has no class selectors, so web's ':hover .reminder-…' rules become the kit's :group-hover on the list-item group, for the checkbox colour and the icon backgrounds.

Platform services and kit colours: open-link, copy and print go through the shell, clipboard and environment services (print hidden where the host cannot print), and the note colour is a data colour with its alpha in the hex code because the kit has no alpha() from @theme-ui/color. The ':hover .note-chip' rule is dropped: desktop has no class selectors, and IconTag draws the chip hover itself.
Only adds the notebook-expand test id that the e2e specs find the tree's expanders by.

Highlighted matches are kit Text with their own background, since the desktop kit has no <span> and no '.match' class selector; the rows give React keys (web leaves them out) and the expand button keeps the search-result-expand test id the e2e specs use.
Drops web's ':hover .trash-chip' rule: desktop has no class selectors, and IconTag draws the chip hover itself.

The list placeholder is centred through ListContainer's placeholderSx (desktop has no '.list-container-placeholder' selector) and ListContainer takes no Scroller; the view keeps the tags test id the e2e specs use.
The crumb hover colour is paragraph: web's paragraph-hover is not a colour in the theme, which the kit's typed colours reject.

List rows resolve without per-row React transitions (useDeferredValue, startTransition), which cut the native renderer's commits per search keystroke from 11 to 6; web uses the @notesnook/common hook with transitions.
